curriculum.lesson_evidence: Communities remember people and events to honour them, to learn from the past and to share an identity. They do this through ceremonies, memorials, minutes of silence, stories and traditions. Different groups may remember different events in different ways.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.child_mission: Communities remember people and events to honour them, to learn from the past and to share an identity. They do this through ceremonies, memorials, minutes of silence, stories and traditions. Different groups may remember different events in different ways.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Why might a town keep a memorial in its main street? Give two reasons.

FEEDBACK
To honour the people named and to remind the community of the past. It also gives people a place to gather and remember together.

WATCH FOR
Thinking memorials are only sad places leaves out honour, learning and shared identity.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Study a local memorial by visiting with an adult or using a photo or council page. Record what it remembers, who it is for, the symbols on it and when it is used. Write three reasons the community keeps it.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Communities remember people and events to honour them, to learn from the past and to share an identity. They do this through ceremonies, memorials, minutes of silence, stories and traditions. Different groups may remember different events in different ways.
materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
